proof: Stable event IDs are derived from tenant, producer, component, probe kind, and probe window.
Two monitor replicas sharing one state path retain one telemetry intent per stable observation window.
HTTP 503 and network failures retry with the identical body and event ID; bounded attempts transition to DLQ.
A telemetry 409 denotes a producer payload conflict and enters DLQ rather than being reported as success.
Missing service identity fails closed and probe/delivery failures do not propagate into active BFF request handlers.
Telemetry, incident create, and incident resolve outbox records retain the same source event ID and dependency ordering.
Incident mappings are not cleared until an incidents-authority response confirms resolution.
SQLite WAL persists probe windows, target state, error windows, delivery claims, DLQ state, incident mappings, and replay audit.
A restarted monitor reads the failed target and its incident mapping from the shared store.
A real local HTTP target was observed healthy, stopped and unavailable, restarted, and recovered; final real IncidentCase authority proof remains dependency-blocked.
The initializer preserves a pre-L12 delivery_outbox as a legacy table and migrates its pending, delivered, and DLQ receipts instead of deleting runtime state.
Exact DLQ replay is operator-only, MFA-bound, approval-referenced, reason-bound, and durably audited.
The controller grants no broker, order, allocation, runtime-control, or live-capital authority.

environment_boundary.proof: Only dev integration and bounded local nonprod tests were exercised; no production or live runtime was changed.

hosted_frontend.proof: This BFF-only task does not change the frontend or its hosting.

mfa.proof: POST /bff/v5/downstream-health/dlq/replay requires verified MFA in addition to operator write authority.

no_live_capital.proof: The health controller and infrastructure event contain no runtime, order, broker, portfolio, capital, strategy, artifact, or execution authority.

rbac.proof: Infrastructure telemetry requires service identity and tenant/producer scope; DLQ replay requires operator-level write authority, MFA, approval_ref, and reason.

tenant_isolation.proof: The exact configured tenant is included in stable identity, persistence keys, telemetry headers, and replay audit; missing tenant authority fails closed.

two_person_approval.proof: Owner Codex2 and reviewer Claude are distinct. Independent approval is pending and is not asserted in this evidence cut.

acceptance.statement: Health telemetry is admitted by the authoritative infrastructure schema without fake RuntimeBinding identity.
Interval probes and error-rate spikes cover the complete configured downstream registry, including newly configured owners.
Probe failures, delivery backlog, incident mapping, and replay audit survive BFF restart and shared replicas.
Telemetry and incident delivery use bounded retry, DLQ, exact governed replay, dependency ordering, and shared source event IDs.
